alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Five courses37.5EC differ in each direction. The first develops epidemiology, infection/immunity, neurobiology, perception/action and patient-health psychology; the second develops programming, linear algebra, numerical methods, image processing and neural networks. Shared biomedical laboratory/disease and introductory physical foundations support coherent but different research priorities.

No degree-title-only rejection; no forced third.

notes.text: TU/e MWT joins medical and life sciences to organic chemistry, physics, mechanobiology, materials, biological-system modelling and staged engineering projects. UCR offers molecular and cellular biology, human physiology and disease, laboratory methods, introductory physical and chemical experiments and quantitative study. The data option adds computational imaging methods. Neither reproduces the full specialist engineering laboratories or compulsory biomedical final project. The UCR computational courses do not guarantee clinical datasets or clinical training.

audience.programmeDescription: TU/e Medical Sciences and Engineering studies molecular and cellular processes in health and disease and uses technology to investigate biomedical problems. Its MWT core combines biological and chemical science with mathematics, physics, laboratory skills and engineering projects.
audience.comparisonExplanation: TU/e MWT joins medical and life sciences to organic chemistry, physics, mechanobiology, materials, biological-system modelling and staged engineering projects. UCR offers molecular and cellular biology, human physiology and disease, laboratory methods, introductory physical and chemical experiments and quantitative study. The data option adds computational imaging methods. Neither reproduces the full specialist engineering laboratories or compulsory biomedical final project. The UCR computational courses do not guarantee clinical datasets or clinical training.
